subject.title: fix(qa): reject runtime tool intent without result evidence

question: Should the QA contract intentionally treat apply-patch, bash, edit, exec, fs-list, fs-read, fs-write, and grep as secondary Codex-native diagnostics rather than required primary runtime-tool coverage?
rationale: The implementation correctly makes result evidence authoritative, but only maintainers can set the desired assurance boundary between OpenClaw dynamic-tool parity and Codex-native workspace behavior.

options.title: Approve the narrower primary gate
options.body: Accept result-backed primary coverage for the four shared product-tool rows and retain the eight Codex-native workspace rows as secondary diagnostics.

options.title: Require a native Codex gate
options.body: Keep this evidence repair but add a separate required validation lane that proves the eight native workspace behaviors through Codex-native result artifacts.

options.title: Retain the old required classification
options.body: Keep the eight rows primary only if their existing fixtures can be upgraded to capture equivalent successful result evidence in both runtimes.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrower primary gate
recommendation.body: Accept result-backed primary coverage for the four shared product-tool rows and retain the eight Codex-native workspace rows as secondary diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the persisted-result and runtime-pair execution architecture that defines this QA contract.
